entries.proposition: Epilepsy-like phenotype is knockout-specific: spontaneous spike-wave discharges with behavioural arrest occur in Neuroligin 2 knockout mice and not in wild-type, Neuroligin 1 or Neuroligin 3 knockout mice; systemic ethosuximide abolished the discharges in all tested knockouts with a vehicle control showing no effect. The restriction is to the animals that have the discharges.
entries.snippet: ETX abolished SWDs in all tested mice whereas control vehicle had no effect (Fig. 2a).
entries.anchor: Results, NLG2 KO mice exhibit SWDs and behavior arrests

entries.proposition: Behavioural effects were assessed in the same animals before and after ethosuximide (open field, elevated plus maze, three-chamber social test), which improved locomotion, anxiety-like measures and social recognition memory in the knockouts. The Methods describe tests 30 min before and after the injection; no vehicle-injected behavioural group is described, so practice and injection effects are not separated from drug effect in these before-and-after comparisons.
entries.snippet: For the ETX treatment, tests were done 30 min prior to and after the systemic or local injection.

entries.proposition: A drug-by-genotype design with several comparison genotypes: ethosuximide had no effect on locomotion, anxiety or social recognition memory in wild-type mice, and did not rescue the social memory deficit of two other autism-related models (PAK3 transgenic; FMR1 knockout) that lack absence seizures. The authors conclude ethosuximide acts in the Neuroligin 2 knockout through blocking the discharges. Group sizes and statistics for these controls are in the supplementary figures that were not opened here.
entries.snippet: To test the possibility that ETX might ameliorate the behavioral deficits of NLG2 KO mice through mechanisms independent of the SWDs, we first performed ETX injection experiments in WT mice but found that ETX had no effects on locomotion, anxiety and social recognition memory
entries.anchor: Results, ETX alleviates behavior deficits in NLG2 KO mice

entries.proposition: Local delivery points to the thalamus: ethosuximide or diazepam injected into the ventrobasal thalamus, but not the cortex, diminished the discharges, partially, and the authors give drug diffusion as the explanation for incomplete blockade; other brain regions may contribute.
entries.snippet: the SWDs appear to originate from or at least critically depend on the thalamus because local injections of ETX or diazepam to the thalamus, but not to the cortex, diminished the SWDs.

entries.proposition: Self-stated limit on mechanism: the partial rescue leaves open that ethosuximide acts through other mechanisms independent of the discharges, and the study does not test T-type channels; diazepam (a GABA-A modulator) also blocks the discharges in the knockout, so a drug effect on the discharges does not itself identify the target.
entries.snippet: we cannot rule out the possibility that ETX may also act through other mechanisms independent of the SWDs and/or other brain regions also contribute to these behavioral deficits in NLG2 KO mice.

entries.proposition: Figure 5 read as an image: panels a and b show knockout mice (n about 11 to 13) before and after ethosuximide with stars on total distance, speed, mobile time, freezing time, open-arm time and entries; panels c and d show sociability (S1 versus empty) unchanged in both genotypes and the novel-mouse preference (S2 versus S1) restored in knockouts after the drug (ns before, ** after) while wild type is a clear preference before and after; panel e local thalamic injection raises distance and mobile time. The plots are before and after points on the same animals without a vehicle arm.
